newsitem.title: UK: Fixtures main feature on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Fixtures main feature on sugar freight market.

text.p: Fixtures were the principal feature of activity on London's sugar freight market with various origins quoted, shipbrokers said on Thursday.

Genoc quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maputo to London for June 7/13 and was said to be on subjects with a further 14,000 tonnes from Cuba to Black Sea with Baltic and Black Sea options for mid-June.
Zimbabwe Sugar Sales also fixed a 17,000-tonne bulk cargo on the Maputo-London run for June 1/10, at a rate believed to be $22.00 on the "Jenny D".
Shipbrokers said South Africa Sugar Association (SASA) fixed 36,000 tonnes in bulk from Durban to Jeddah but details of the rate have yet to emerge.
Jean Lion fixed 13,500 tonnes from Thailand to south China at $16.50 but more details were unavailable.
In other firmer business, shipbrokers said Czarnikow was on subjects with its inquiry for 12/13,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to east Africa for June 5/10.
E D & F Man was also on subjects with 13,750 tonnes in bags from east coast Mexico to Chittagong, they said.

In other news, an early forecast for special preferential imports of raw cane sugar from ACP countries into the EU was put at 300,000 tonnes for 1997/98 on Wednesday compared with 296,000 tonnes last year.
